correction: They solve team and deployment coupling and usually cost performance.
Microfrontends is an architecture; Module Federation is one of several ways to compose the parts.

belief: One composition technique covers every requirement.
correction: Each technique satisfies some requirements (independent deploy, shared state, style isolation, SEO) and not others.

belief: The host bundles the remote into its own build.
correction: The remote is fetched at runtime from its own deployment.

belief: The browser fetches the host and the remote in parallel from the start.
correction: The host runs first and learns about the remote afterwards, so requests can come in sequence.
Sharing happens only for packages declared in the shared configuration, and sub-path imports need their own entries.

belief: Two copies of React on a page are harmless.
correction: React lists more than one copy as a cause of the invalid hook call warning.

belief: A version mismatch on a shared package shows up as an obvious error.
correction: What the runtime does on a mismatch depends on the configuration; the lesson records it from the example project.

belief: A remote can change its exports freely.
correction: The host depends on the exposed names and shapes; a change that compiles in the remote can break the host at runtime.

belief: Each remote can manage the URL as if it were the only app on the page.
correction: The browser has one URL, so one part must own it and the others work inside the share they are given.

belief: A link into the middle of a remote works like any other link.
correction: On a cold start the shell must load the remote before the inner route can render.

belief: A shared global store is the easy answer for communication.
correction: A shared store couples deploys, because its shape becomes a contract between teams.

belief: CSS written in one remote only affects that remote.
correction: A global rule applies to the whole document unless something isolates it.
Each isolation option costs something, such as naming discipline, build setup or limits on theming.

belief: Deploying a remote on its own cannot break the other parts.
correction: The host loads the latest remote at runtime, so a bad release or an outage reaches users unless the host handles it.

belief: A new remote release reaches users at once.
correction: A cached entry file can keep serving an older build; releases need a cache strategy.

belief: Sharing dependencies and splitting into remotes cost nothing at runtime.
correction: Duplicate dependencies, chained loading and extra requests are the price; preloading and sharing change how much is paid.
